items.abstract: <jats:p>Wind Power Forecasting (WPF) serves as a critical enabler for the secure integration of wind energy into modern power systems, supporting efficient grid dispatch and electricity market operations. Despite significant advancements in data-driven forecasting methods, particularly deep learning models, existing studies often rely on experiments conducted on limited scenarios using private datasets, with inconsistent configurations in input sequence length, forecast horizon, and meteorological data resolution. This leads to poor comparability across methods, difficulties in reproducing forecasting results, and inadequate assessment of model robustness and generalization capabilities. To address these gaps, we propose WPF-Bench, a comprehensive and extensible benchmark framework designed for the systematic evaluation of mainstream models. WPF-Bench integrates 7 real-world datasets comprising approximately 3.68 million hours of data from diverse climatic and topographical environments across multiple continents. It facilitates the evaluation of multi-scale forecasting under various configurations, alongside assessments of cross-site zero-shot and probabilistic forecasting. Built upon a unified climate data source and a standardized preprocessing pipeline, WPF-Bench enforces consistent experimental protocols for data splitting, normalization, and covariate handling, ensuring fair and reproducible performance comparisons across more than 20 deep learning models. In summary, we provide unified standardized data, a comprehensive and fair multi-scenario evaluation platform, and empirical insights into model strengths and limitations across diverse scenarios, to advance the development of innovative architectures and the implementation of robust, generalizable WPF methods.</jats:p>
title: WPF-Bench: A Comprehensive Multi-Scenario Benchmark for Deep Learning in Wind Power Forecasting
